The two reciprocal pairs, A and B and C and D, are drawn in the accent color: four of the seven arcs have a partner pointing back, so reciprocity is 4 / 7 = 0.571." width="100%"} Reciprocity measures the proportion of edges in a directed graph that are bidirectional (mutual). Returns a value between `0.0` (no reciprocal edges) and `1.0` (all edges are reciprocal). This metric is fundamental for understanding relationship symmetry in social networks, mutual influence in citation networks, and bidirectional flows in transportation or communication networks. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["default"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Calculation mode for reciprocity. Can either be `"default"` or `"ratio"`, where the latter is `(# mutual edges) / (total # edges)`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Reciprocity value between `0.0` and `1.0`, or `0.0` for empty graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on an undirected graph or with invalid mode. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Out of 3 edges, 2 form a mutual pair (`A<->B`) and 1 is one-directional (`A->C`), giving a reciprocity of 2/3: ::: {#7b8b8206 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), # Mutual with above ("A", "C"), # No reciprocal ] ) ) # Returns 0.667 (2 mutual out of 3 edges) graph.reciprocity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.6666666666666666 ``` ::: ::: A tightly-knit friend group where every connection goes both ways has a reciprocity of exactly 1.0, while a one-way "followers" network has a reciprocity of 0.0: ::: {#cfde3ceb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} friendship = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) # Returns 1.0: every edge has a reciprocal counterpart friendship.reciprocity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: :::
